literal: Prince of Guangyang Shi Hou died.
idiomatic: Shi Hou, Prince of Guangyang, died.

literal: Third month, day bingxu: an edict stated: "We think on the hundred surnames' illness and suffering; many among the people meet untimely death; clear dawn finds no sleep; guilt weighs on the heart and pain racks the head.
idiomatic: In the third month, on the bingxu day, an edict stated, "We think on the people's illness and suffering; many among them meet untimely death; from clear dawn we find no sleep; guilt weighs on our heart and pain racks our head.

literal: Therefore We broadly gather skilled physicians and gather famous drugs from afar, wishing thereby to succor the myriad people.
idiomatic: Therefore we broadly gather skilled physicians and gather famous drugs from afar, wishing thereby to succor the myriad people.

literal: This may be proclaimed throughout the realm: when the people have illness, the local offices are to send physicians to visit their homes and diagnose them; needed drugs are to be supplied by the physicians as they judge fit."
idiomatic: This may be proclaimed throughout the realm: when the people have illness, the local offices are to send physicians to visit their homes and diagnose them; needed drugs are to be supplied by the physicians as they judge fit."

literal: Summer, fourth month, day xinchou: a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the xinchou day, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

literal: Day wushen: Changsun Guan's army reached Mantou Mountain, greatly defeated Shibin; Shibin with several hundred horsemen of his retinue fled by night; Shibin's younger cousin Douwulai and his chieftains Pilouba, Lei, and others led their followers to surrender.
idiomatic: On the wushen day Changsun Guan's army reached Mantou Mountain and greatly defeated Shibin; Shibin fled by night with several hundred horsemen of his retinue; his younger cousin Douwulai and chieftains including Pilouba and Lei led their followers to surrender.

literal: Fifth month: the imperial younger brother Changle was enfeoffed as Prince of Jianchang.
idiomatic: In the fifth month the imperial younger brother Changle was enfeoffed as Prince of Jianchang.

literal: Sixth month: Liu Yu sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the sixth month Liu Yu sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Autumn, eighth month: bandits entered Pengcheng, killed the garrison commander Yuan Jiechou; the chief clerk led troops and destroyed them.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn bandits entered Pengcheng, killed the garrison commander Yuan Jiechou, and the chief clerk led troops and destroyed them.

literal: The Rouran raided the frontier.
idiomatic: The Rouran raided the frontier.

literal: Ninth month, day bingyin: the imperial carriage campaigned north; the generals all assembled at Nüshui and greatly defeated the barbarian hosts.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the bingyin day, the court campaigned north; the generals all assembled at Nüshui and greatly defeated the barbarian hosts.

literal: The matter is fully set forth in the Rouran Annals.
idiomatic: The matter is fully set forth in the Rouran Annals.

literal: Minister of the Masses, Prince of Dong'an Liu Ni was dismissed for an offense.
idiomatic: Liu Ni, Minister of the Masses and Prince of Dong'an, was dismissed for an offense.

literal: Day renshen: the imperial carriage returned from the northern campaign; a drinking ceremony was held and merit was recorded; report was made at the ancestral temple.
idiomatic: On the renshen day the court returned from the northern campaign; a drinking ceremony was held, merit was recorded, and report was made at the ancestral temple.

literal: Winter, tenth month: Prince of Jinan Murong Baiyao and Prince of Gaoping Li Fu were executed.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Murong Baiyao, Prince of Jinan, and Li Fu, Prince of Gaoping, were executed.

literal: Eleventh month: an edict relaxed prohibitions on mountains and marshes.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month an edict relaxed prohibitions on mountains and marshes.

literal: Twelfth month, day jiachen: the court visited Luye Park and the stone cave temple.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the jiachen day, the court visited Luye Park and the stone cave temple.

literal: Prince of Yangping Xincheng died.
idiomatic: Xincheng, Prince of Yangping, died.

literal: Fifth year, spring, third month, day yihai: an edict stated: "Since Tian'an, military and state affairs have been many; in the south Xu was pacified, in the north remnant barbarians were swept away.
idiomatic: In the third month of spring of the fifth year, on the yihai day, an edict stated, "Since Tian'an, military and state affairs have been many; in the south Xu was pacified, in the north remnant barbarians were swept away.

literal: Men on campaign and garrison have fled and scattered in no small number; though their crimes fit the penal code, We have repeatedly shown compassionate pardon.
idiomatic: Men on campaign and garrison have fled and scattered in no small number; though their crimes fit the penal code, we have repeatedly shown compassionate pardon.

literal: Yet lenient government is like water, and fugitives have accordingly grown many.
idiomatic: Yet lenient government is like water, and fugitives have accordingly grown many.

literal: It is fitting to clarify the canonical punishments to awe treachery and fraud.
idiomatic: It is fitting to clarify the canonical punishments to awe treachery and fraud.

literal: From now on all fugitive soldiers and outgoing magistrates and garrison commanders who roam and do not report are, by the thirtieth day of the sixth month, all permitted to surrender; those who do not surrender are to be judged according to law."
idiomatic: From now on all fugitive soldiers and outgoing magistrates and garrison commanders who roam and do not report are, by the thirtieth day of the sixth month, all permitted to surrender; those who do not surrender are to be judged according to law."

literal: " An edict that Acting Palace Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Xing You was envoy to Liu Yu.
idiomatic: An edict named Xing You, Acting Palace Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, envoy to Liu Yu.

literal: The text is deficient.
idiomatic: The text is deficient.

literal: Summer, fourth month: the western Tiele rebelled; an edict that Prince of Ruyin Tiansi and Palace Attendant Giving Luo Yun were to campaign against them.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer the western Tiele rebelled; an edict ordered Tiansi, Prince of Ruyin, and Luo Yun, palace attendant giving, to campaign against them.

literal: Yun was attacked and killed by the Tiele; the dead were five or six in ten.
idiomatic: Luo Yun was attacked and killed by the Tiele; five or six in ten of his men died.

literal: Prince of Beiping Changsun Dun died.
idiomatic: Changsun Dun, Prince of Beiping, died.

literal: Sixth month, day dingwei: the court traveled to Hexi.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the dingwei day, the court traveled to Hexi.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day bingyin: then reached Yinshan.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the bingyin day, the court then reached Yinshan.

literal: Eighth month, day dinghai: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the dinghai day, the court returned to the palace.

literal: The Emperor by nature held worldly affairs in light esteem and often had a mind to leave the world; he wished to abdicate the throne to his paternal uncle, Prince of Jingzhao Zitui—the account is in the Biography of Prince of Rencheng Yun—and when the ministers firmly petitioned, the Emperor then desisted.
idiomatic: The emperor by nature held worldly affairs in light esteem and often had a mind to leave the world; he wished to abdicate the throne to his paternal uncle Zitui, Prince of Jingzhao—the account is in the Biography of Prince of Rencheng Yun—and when the ministers firmly petitioned, he desisted.

literal: Day bingwu: the investiture edict to the crown prince stated: "Of old when Yao and Shun ceded the realm to all under Heaven, it was because their sons were unworthy.
idiomatic: On the bingwu day the investiture edict to the crown prince stated, "Of old when Yao and Shun ceded the realm to all under Heaven, it was because their sons were unworthy.

literal: If Danzhu and Shangjun could bear the burden, how would they have sought out the obscure and lowly to confer it?
idiomatic: If Danzhu and Shangjun could bear the burden, how would they have sought out the obscure and lowly to confer it?

literal: Though you are young and tender, you have the bearing of a ruler; you will surely be able to restore and exalt the kingly Way and thereby succor the myriad people.
idiomatic: Though you are young and tender, you have the bearing of a ruler; you will surely be able to restore and exalt the kingly Way and thereby succor the myriad people.

literal: Now We send the Grand Tutor, Prince of Jian'an Lu Fu, and Grand Commandant Yuan He, bearing the staff of authority, to present the imperial seal and cord and transfer the position to your person.
idiomatic: Now we send Lu Fu, Grand Tutor and Prince of Jian'an, and Yuan He, Grand Commandant, bearing the staff of authority, to present the imperial seal and cord and transfer the position to your person.

literal: Take up the imperial throne, expand the great enterprise, and brighten the ancestors' glory, that We may roam at ease upon the Way, nourish the spirit and nurture the nature—can this fail to be good?"
idiomatic: Take up the imperial throne, expand the great enterprise, and brighten the ancestors' glory, that we may roam at ease upon the Way, nourish the spirit and nurture the nature—can this fail to be good?"

literal: " Day dingwei: an edict stated: "We inherit the great enterprise; fortune belongs to the age of peace; the Huai and Dai have submitted in succession; within the four seas all is clear and tranquil.
idiomatic: On the dingwei day an edict stated, "We inherit the great enterprise; fortune belongs to an age of peace; the Huai and Dai have submitted in succession; within the four seas all is clear and tranquil.

literal: Therefore We aspire to the remote antiquity of mystery and keep the will stored in simplicity.
idiomatic: Therefore we aspire to the remote antiquity of mystery and keep the will stored in simplicity.

literal: Personally to survey the myriad affairs harms the harmony of nourishing the spirit;
idiomatic: Personally to survey the myriad affairs harms the harmony of nourishing the spirit;

literal: if even one day is neglected, governance suffers the fault of delay and stagnation.
idiomatic: if even one day is neglected, governance suffers the fault of delay and stagnation.

literal: Yet when the son possesses all under Heaven, honor returns to the father;
idiomatic: Yet when the son possesses all under Heaven, honor returns to the father;

literal: when the father possesses all under Heaven, he transmits it to the son.
idiomatic: when the father possesses all under Heaven, he transmits it to the son.

literal: Now examining the accord of numinous fortune and testing the hearts of the multitude, We command the heir apparent to ascend the great throne.
idiomatic: Now examining the accord of numinous fortune and testing the hearts of the multitude, we command the heir apparent to ascend the great throne.

literal: We shall roam at ease in reverent self-restraint, lodge the heart in vast clarity; the altars of state are at peace and the enterprise is broadly expanded—is this not good?"
idiomatic: We shall roam at ease in reverent self-restraint and lodge the heart in vast clarity; the altars of state are at peace and the enterprise is broadly expanded—is this not good?"

literal: All officials and offices are to reverently serve the heir, in answer to Heaven's blessing.
idiomatic: All officials and offices are to reverently serve the heir, in answer to Heaven's blessing.

literal: Proclaim it within the realm that all may hear and know.
idiomatic: Proclaim it within the realm that all may hear and know.

literal: " Thereupon the assembled dukes memorialized: "Of old in the age of the Three Sovereigns, simplicity and nonaction prevailed; therefore they were styled 'sovereigns.'
idiomatic: Thereupon the assembled dukes memorialized, "Of old in the age of the Three Sovereigns, simplicity and nonaction prevailed; therefore they were styled 'sovereigns.'

literal: Thus when Han Gaozu had already styled himself emperor, he honored his father as Supreme Emperor, making clear that he did not rule all under Heaven.
idiomatic: Thus when Han Gaozu had already styled himself emperor, he honored his father as Supreme Emperor, making clear that he did not rule all under Heaven.

literal: Now the emperor is young and tender; the myriad affairs and great policies still ought to be overseen by Your Majesty.
idiomatic: Now the emperor is young and tender; the myriad affairs and great policies still ought to be overseen by Your Majesty.

literal: We respectfully offer the honorific title Supreme Emperor."
idiomatic: We respectfully offer the honorific title Supreme Emperor."

literal: " He then assented.
idiomatic: He then assented.

literal: Day jiyou: the Supreme Emperor moved his residence to Chongguang Palace; rafters were taken unhewn and there were only earthen steps.
idiomatic: On the jiyou day the Supreme Emperor moved his residence to Chongguang Palace; rafters were taken unhewn and there were only earthen steps.

literal: All great affairs of state were reported to him.
idiomatic: All great affairs of state were reported to him.

literal: First year of Chengming, age twenty-three, he died in Yong'an Hall; the posthumous honorific title Emperor Xianwen was offered; temple name Xianzu; burial at Jinling in Yunzhong.
idiomatic: In the first year of Chengming, at the age of twenty-three, he died in Yong'an Hall; the posthumous honorific title Emperor Xianwen was offered; temple name Xianzu; burial at Jinling in Yunzhong.

literal: The historiographer states: Quick and perceptive from youth, combining talent with decisive judgment—is this not what is meant by Xianzu?
idiomatic: The historiographer states: Quick and perceptive from youth, combining talent with decisive judgment—is this not what is meant by Xianzu?

literal: Therefore he could further clarify the desert wilds and greatly open the southern domains.
idiomatic: Therefore he could further clarify the desert wilds and greatly open the southern domains.

literal: Yet early he harbored a mind weary of the world and in the end brought palace turmoil—is it Heaven's will?
idiomatic: Yet early he harbored a mind weary of the world and in the end brought palace turmoil—is it Heaven's will?

literal: Collation notes
idiomatic: Collation notes

literal: Making the outgoing administration select officials to await the worthy and able: Beishi juan 2, Wei Ji 2, Cefu juan 156
idiomatic: Making the outgoing administration select officials to await the worthy and able: Beishi juan 2, Wei Ji 2, Cefu juan 156

literal: 〈page 1889〉
reads "worthy and able" as "successors."
idiomatic: reads "worthy and able" as "successors."

literal: According to this, "successors" means the officials who succeed to office—namely that the outgoing administration
idiomatic: According to this, "successors" means the officials who succeed to office—namely that the outgoing administration

idiomatic: (outgoing administration)

idiomatic: selects officials to leave for the succeeding officials.

literal: Viewing the edict's meaning before and after, it should read "successors."
idiomatic: Viewing the edict's meaning before and after, it should read "successors."

idiomatic: Cefu, excerpting the Book of Wei, agrees with Beishi; this also proves the Wei Shu original likewise read "successors."

literal: Khitan, Jufufu, Yuyuling, Rilian, Pili'er, Chiliushou, Ximandan, A'dahe, Yuzhenhou, Khotan, Persia, and other states each sent envoys with tribute: the states listed here, apart from Khotan and Persia, all appear in juan 100, Biographies of the Wuji, and the Khitan Annals, but the annals and biographies both differ and the two biographies do not agree; for now we mark the breaks according to the Wuji Annals; "Jufufu" in the annals, the Wuji Annals read "Jufuvu."
idiomatic: Khitan, Jufufu, Yuyuling, Rilian, Pili'er, Chiliushou, Ximandan, A'dahe, Yuzhenhou, Khotan, Persia, and other states each sent envoys with tribute: the states listed here, apart from Khotan and Persia, all appear in juan 100, Biographies of the Wuji, and the Khitan Annals, but the annals and biographies both differ and the two biographies do not agree; for now we mark the breaks according to the Wuji Annals; "Jufufu" in the annals, the Wuji Annals read "Jufuvu."

idiomatic: "Chiliushou" appears only in the Khitan Annals, where it reads "Tuliuyu"; the annals are suspected to be in error.

idiomatic: "A'dahe River": the Wuji Annals read "Badahé"; the Khitan Annals read "Hedahé"; the Wuji Annals are probably in error.

idiomatic: As for mutual differences between the two biographies, see the collation notes to juan 100; they are not all set forth here.

literal: Edict that Acting Palace Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Xing You was envoy to Liu Yu: Beishi juan 2 records this matter on the yihai day of the second month of that year; following the text above, this would be the yihai day of the third month.
idiomatic: Edict that Acting Palace Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Xing You was envoy to Liu Yu: Beishi juan 2 records this matter on the yihai day of the second month of that year; following the text above, this would be the yihai day of the third month.

literal: According to this, in the second month of that year the new moon was on day jichou; there was no yihai day; it seems "third month" is correct.
idiomatic: According to this, in the second month of that year the new moon was on day jichou; there was no yihai day; it seems "third month" is correct.

idiomatic: Yet the Annals of Emperor Ming in Song Shu juan 8, seventh year of Taishi

idiomatic: states, "Third month, day xinyou, the northern barbarians sent envoys presenting local products."

idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian juan 133

takes this to be the mission of Xing You recorded in this annal.

idiomatic: Examining this: in the third month of that year the new moon was on day jiwei; xinyou was the third day and yihai the seventeenth—how could Song have received envoys before Wei had yet dispatched them?

idiomatic: If one holds that what Song Shu records is a separate mission, then within so short a span, without special cause, frequent dispatch of envoys is impossible.
